# pidginhost_kubernetes_lb_firewall (Resource)

The firewall rules of the load balancer of a Kubernetes cluster. The rule list is authoritative: rules the load balancer has that are not listed are deleted, and destroying the resource deletes all rules.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Lists every rule of the cluster load balancer: rules missing here are deleted.
resource "pidginhost_kubernetes_lb_firewall" "example" {
  cluster_id = pidginhost_kubernetes_cluster.example.id

  rule = [
    {
      direction = "in"
      action    = "ACCEPT"
      protocol  = "tcp"
      source    = "203.0.113.0/24"
      dport     = "443"
      comment   = "office"
    },
    {
      direction = "in"
      action    = "DROP"
      protocol  = "tcp"
      dport     = "443"
      position  = 200
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) ID of the Kubernetes cluster. Changing it replaces the object.

### Optional

- `rule` (Attributes List) Rules of the load balancer. The list is authoritative: rules the load balancer has but the list does not are deleted. Rules match existing ones on direction, action, protocol, addresses and ports; comment, enabled and position change in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as cluster_id.

<a id="nestedatt--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `action` (String) Action for matching traffic: ACCEPT, DROP or REJECT.
- `direction` (String) Traffic direction: in or out.

Optional:

- `comment` (String) Free text comment.
- `destination` (String) Destination IP address or CIDR.
- `dport` (String) Destination port or range, such as 80 or 8000-9000.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is active. Defaults to true.
- `position` (Number) Rule order, lower runs first. Defaults to 100.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol, such as tcp, udp or icmp. Required with sport or dport.
- `source` (String) Source IP address or CIDR.
- `sport` (String) Source port or range, such as 1024-65535.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import the load balancer rules of a cluster by the cluster ID.
terraform import pidginhost_kubernetes_lb_firewall.example 7
```
